questions.q: Where do standard and custom fields appear in an object's settings?
options: In separate tabs — one for standard, one for custom
Mixed together in the same Fields & Relationships list, with no visual separation
Custom fields only appear in Schema Builder
Standard fields are hidden by default
questions.explain: Every object's Fields & Relationships list mixes standard and custom fields together in one table.

questions.q: What can you actually change about a standard field?
options: Its data type, freely
Its label, through Rename Tabs and Labels — while its underlying API name and data type stay fixed
Nothing at all, ever
Only its help text, never its label
questions.explain: A standard field's label can be changed via Rename Tabs and Labels, but its data type and API name remain what Salesforce defined.

questions.q: Why does Step 1 of the New Custom Field wizard offer the entire Data Type menu?
options: Because custom fields can change type after creation anyway
Because nothing about a field that doesn't exist yet is locked in
Because standard fields don't have a Data Type setting
It's a bug — only three types should show
questions.explain: A brand-new custom field hasn't been saved yet, so every data type family is still an open choice on Step 1.

questions.q: What does a custom field's API name always end in?
options: _std
A random number
The word "Custom"
questions.explain: Every custom field's API name ends in __c, a reliable structural tell even without a dedicated indicator column.

questions.q: Which is generally true about deleting a field?
options: Custom fields can be deleted; standard fields almost never can
Standard fields can always be deleted; custom fields cannot
Neither type can ever be deleted
Both types can always be deleted with no restrictions
questions.explain: Custom fields are deletable by an admin; standard fields are, with very rare exceptions, not.
